answers.children: Curly-Coated Retrievers can be good with older children but need careful management around toddlers. Their large size, boundless energy and independent nature mean they may accidentally knock over small children during bursts of excitement while retrieving or problem-solving. Bred as rugged English gun dogs for waterfowl and game, they are affectionate with family on their terms and require respect for their space. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Curly-Coated Retrievers generally get along with other pets when raised together though their independent streak can create tension. As a sporting breed originally developed to retrieve waterfowl and game their prey drive remains present and they may chase smaller animals. With same-sex dogs they can show aloofness or dominance rooted in their discerning temperament towards strangers.
answers.exercise: Curly-Coated Retrievers need at least one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise. Long runs, intense swims or wetland hikes suit their exceptional swimming and retrieving ability developed for harsh English hunting conditions. Without this significant physical and mental stimulation the energetic breed becomes bored and destructive given its intelligent and independent nature.
answers.shedding: Yes — Curly-Coated Retrievers shed moderately with tight water-resistant curls that trap loose hair and require regular checks. Their short curly coat evolved to protect them from icy waters and brambles during hunts for waterfowl and game so it releases curls that can scatter around the house especially after swimming or fieldwork.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic yet the Curly-Coated Retriever is sometimes suggested for allergy sufferers because its short curly coat produces less loose hair than many sporting breeds. The tight water-resistant curls still shed moderately and need grooming to prevent mats so dander can still be present in the home.
answers.training: Curly-Coated Retrievers are relatively easy to train thanks to their high intelligence and problem-solving nature. Their independent streak from English gun dog ancestry means they may test boundaries or choose their own solutions rather than await direction making consistent mental challenges essential for this energetic breed.
answers.lifespan: Curly-Coated Retrievers live 10-14 years. Their rugged build and stamina from retrieving waterfowl and game in harsh English conditions support this range though the breed's health robustness depends on providing the significant physical and mental stimulation its intelligent and energetic temperament demands to avoid stress-related issues over time.
answers.size: Curly-Coated Retrievers reach 60-95 lb and stand 23-27 in tall as adults. Their large powerful build with substance for swimming through icy waters and pushing through brambles feels substantial in the home requiring owners to manage their strength during play or when the independent breed decides to investigate something interesting on its own.
answers.barking: Curly-Coated Retrievers do not bark excessively. Their discerning and often aloof temperament with strangers leads them to stay quiet unless there is a clear reason tied to their original role retrieving waterfowl and game in England where unnecessary noise would have been undesirable during hunts.
answers.apartment: Curly-Coated Retrievers are not well suited to apartment living. Their boundless energy intelligent problem-solving nature and need for one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise mean they struggle to settle indoors without constant mental stimulation and can become destructive if their independent streak is not matched by an active lifestyle.
answers.first-time: Curly-Coated Retrievers are not ideal as a first dog. Their high intelligence combined with an independent streak and requirement for significant physical and mental stimulation from their English gun dog history can overwhelm novices who may not match the energetic breed's problem-solving schemes or need for purposeful activity.
